summary: Prolonged pre-stream pause for chat responses after runtime/model compatibility rollout in eu-west
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an observable 600-1200ms pause between the chat completion request and the first streamed token after our runtime/model compatibility rollout (Runtime 2.1 + model handoff) in eu-west. This pause appears before any streaming chunks are delivered; subsequent streaming token cadence is normal. Impact: multiple production customers (dedicated pools) experiencing degraded perceived latency for assistant responses which affects UI UX for conversational products.

Impact:
- Median TTFB for affected customer increased from ~80ms to ~720ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens).
- P95 TTFB rose to ~1.2s during the initial 30 minutes after rollout for eu-west-serving clusters.
- Customers on dedicated capacity see the effect; shared hosted customers in the same region not consistently affected.

Environment:
- Prod eu-west dedicated pools (customer-specific capacity)
- Runtime: 2.1.0 (rolled out 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC)
- Model variants: redwood-7b-v2 (quantized), open-llama-13b-quant (fallback)
- API path: /v1/chat/completions with streaming=true

Expected behavior:
- Minimal pre-stream handshake (<=150ms median) and steady streaming cadence after first token.

Actual behavior:
- Single, consistent pause (600-1200ms) before first streaming chunk; follow-on token throughput normal.

Reproducibility:
- Reproducible for affected dedicated pools using same prompt and model pinning. Not reproducible from global hosted test accounts in us-east.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated API key pinned to a dedicated pool in eu-west
2) Call POST /v1/chat/completions with streaming=true and a short system+user prompt (<= 64 tokens total), model pinned to redwood-7b-v2
3) Measure time from request accept to first streamed chunk (first token) and compare to pre-2.1 baseline
4) Observe consistent ~600-1200ms pause before first token in affected pools

Serving runtime trace id: sr_9f8b7 (attached traces in Kibana)
Model load logs show no cold-start events; KV cache hit-rate normal for pinned sessions
No 5xx or throttling events in the API gateway during observed window
metrics: No appreciable change in tokens/sec after first token
CPU/GPU utilization on affected nodes: GPU 42-58%, CPU 18-25% (no saturation)
investigation_notes: 03/12 04:00 - Support: Confirmed multiple customer reports for eu-west dedicated pools. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE.
03/12 04:18 - SRE: Reviewed Grafana TTFB panel (dash/ttfb-eu-west). Spike correlates with runtime 2.1 canary -> full rollout window. No obvious resource exhaustion.

03/12 04:35 - Eng (runtime): Noted a small change in the session negotiation handshake in 2.1 that adds an extra capability negotiation round-trip when model/ABI mismatch is detected. Hypothesis: capability-negotiation path incurring synchronous wait before streaming begins in dedicated pools when model variant selection triggers a compatibility check.
03/12 05:05 - Additional testing: Forcing fallback to open-llama-13b-quant in same pool reduced pre-stream pause to ~120ms, suggesting the issue is on the redwood-7b-v2 compatibility path.

03/12 05:40 - Found traces where the runtime performs an extra serialize/deserialize compatibility check (~500-800ms) before allocating decoder stream. This check is executed serially on the request path for certain model ABI signatures in dedicated pools.
03/12 06:10 - Mitigation tested: Toggle runtime flag runtime.skip_compat_check_for_pinned=true on a canary dedicated pool -> immediate reduction in TTFB to ~100ms for the same requests.
